shorts.title: Off Iceland, Pilot Whales Move In and the Orcas Leave
shorts.outro: Doug tries to keep up with those orcas in the full video below.
shorts.description: Fourteen years of Icelandic sightings show long-finned pilot whales moving in on killer whales and the killer whales almost always moving away, sometimes porpoising at high speed; Doug tries to keep up in the full episode linked above.

shorts.title: An Orca Was Seen Swimming With a Newborn Pilot Whale
shorts.outro: Doug meets the calf's very large family in the full video below.
shorts.description: In August 2021 off western Iceland, researchers watched a female killer whale named Sædís swim for 21 minutes with a newborn long-finned pilot whale tucked in beside her, and the full episode linked above explains what scientists think about these two species.

shorts.title: 4 of 5 Pilot Whales Swam Toward Recorded Orca Calls
shorts.outro: Doug finds that speaker, in an orca costume, in the full video below.
shorts.description: In a playback study off northern Norway, most tagged pilot whales turned toward recorded killer whale calls while other whales had moved away from them; Doug finds that speaker in the full episode linked above.
